title: AES 8-round JNP14: aes-8r-known-key-remove-first-jnp2014

target.description: 8 complete AES-like rounds with known expanded AES round keys and MixColumns in every round, including the last. Table 2 standard-size t=4,c=8 endpoint; remove-first refers to truncating the generic nine-round trail, not deleting an AES key schedule.

setting.key_relation: One fixed fully known AES master key and its known expanded round keys; no related-key access or chosen weak key.
setting.key_population: fixed fully known key; no special weak-key selection
setting.plaintext_model: Find a pair in restricted input/output difference spaces of size 2^32 each.
assumptions: The standard AES dimensions are t=4 and c=8; round keys are incorporated as known constants.
List-merging analysis uses the stated uniformity assumption for S-box-induced list partitions.
Complete journal audit confirms known fixed round keys and finalMixColumns. Printed788 conditionT>=C is a local comparison-sign typo; Table2 values56/56/32 versusgeneric64 are unchanged.
setting.reference_model: Known-key restricted differential pair-finding versus a random 128-bit permutation with input/output difference-space sizes IN=OUT=2^32; Eq.18 gives generic work 2^64.

time.note: Eq.17 evaluated at the exact published Table 2 assignment.

success.description: No numerical whole restricted-pair-finding success is stated for this eight-round known-key configuration. The merge analysis expects one inbound solution from2^32 assignments under its uniform-list model; this is not certain list existence or successful full-budget output. The conditional2^-24 outbound model does not justify an independent-repetition Poisson recovery curve. Known round keys and a restricted pair output are not secret-key recovery; no generic-reference probability or success normalization is invented.

components.description: Section4.2 first-case list model after choosing the WLOG cheaper orientation: t=4,c=8,min(mB,mF)=1, so one guessed assignment merges with source probability2^(-c*t*1)=2^-32. The source explicitly assumes uniform S-box-induced partitions.2^32 assignments give expected one solution, not a guaranteed nonempty or unique list.

Equation16 and the two t=4,c=8 eight-round Table2 assignments have nB+nF=5: source outbound product2^(-8*(8-5))=2^-24. Its expected2^24 repetitions remain tied to the same known-key pair-finding construction, not a decision-success distribution.

Existing conflicts, native costs, target variants, settings, parameter assignments and full-audit gates remain unchanged.
